newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU set to challenge Paris on World Cup'98 stadium.
newsitem.headline: EU set to challenge Paris on World Cup'98 stadium.

text.p: France's preparations for the 1998 soccer World Cup face a legal blow on Wednesday, when the the European Commission is due to step up legal moves against Paris's award of contracts to build and run its new stadium.

"The Commission will send a 'reasoned opinion' tomorrow," a Commission source said on Tuesday, meaning France will be hauled before the European Court of Justice in Luxembourg if it fails to put its house in order over the 80,000 seater stadium.

France would have two months to rectify complaints related to the building and operating concessions for its half-built "Grand Stade de France" stadium, being built in northern Paris as the centrepiece of French World Cup plans .

Commission inquiries stem from October 1995, after competing contractors cried foul over the allocation of contracts, accusing successful bidders Bouyges, Dumez and SGE of having changed their bid after its submission.
Other issues include concern about the granting of stadium operating concessions without a tendering procedure.
Work on the stadium, due for completion in November this year, could be put back if France fails to satisfy Commission questions about the 2.67-billion-franc ($487 million) project. ($=5.48 francs)
